domain_claim: canonical_digest(source, contract) deterministically hashes all 17 ResourceContract fields
notes: Primary gap: canonical_digest() currently takes only WorkflowSource, not ResourceContract. Kani can prove determinism for concrete contracts; Verus can prove for-all contract inequality ⇒ digest inequality (with collision probability bound); proptest can fuzz thousands of random contract pairs.

domain_claim: Changing any single ResourceContract field produces a different digest
notes: For each of the 17 fields, changing only that field (keeping others constant) must change the digest. Kani can verify for bounded field values; proptest covers broader random exploration; Flux could refine field relationships.

domain_claim: canonical_digest field encoding prevents cross-field hash collisions
notes: Each field is tagged with a domain string before being hashed (e.g., 'max_steps' + value). This prevents field-permutation collisions where swapping values between fields produces the same hash. Verus can prove the injectivity of the encoding; Kani can check for concrete collision candidates.

domain_claim: canonical_digest produces same output as before for DEFAULT contract IF contract hash is appended after source hash
notes: If we implement digest = hash(old_digest || contract_hash) where old_digest is the current (no-contract) hash, then the new digest = hash(old_value || hash(DEFAULT)). This gives a deterministic migration path. Kani can verify the relationship.

domain_claim: Single canonical ResourceContract type: only one definition exists in the codebase
notes: After merging types, Kani can verify that all 17 fields are accessible from the canonical type. Loom is not directly applicable but mentioned for completeness. This is primarily a compile-time check (type system) + test verification.

domain_claim: All code paths (compile, validate, budget, runtime) use the same ResourceContract type
notes: After type merge, verify that validation/resource.rs, budget.rs, compile/mod.rs, chunk_002.rs all import from the same canonical source. A compile-time test can assert type identity via std::any::TypeId or similar.

domain_claim: Every compilation entry point accepts a ResourceContract parameter (not hardcoded DEFAULT)
notes: Kani can verify that for a non-DEFAULT contract, the resulting CompiledWorkflow.resource_contract() equals the input contract. Proptest can fuzz random contracts through all 6 entry points.

domain_claim: Changing allows_secret_results from false to true changes the canonical digest
notes: Kani: verify digest(allows_secret_results=true) ≠ digest(allows_secret_results=false) for a fixed source. Verus: prove injectivity of bool→digest for the contract hash. Proptest: randomize all other fields, toggle the flag, assert digest difference.

domain_claim: Runtime SecretResultNotAllowed enforcement matches the allows_secret_results value in the contract that was hashed
notes: Kani: verify that when allows_secret_results=false, any answer with Taint::Secret produces Err(SecretResultNotAllowed). Verus: prove that the contract used at runtime is the same one that was hashed during compilation (requires tracking contract through serialization/deserialization).

domain_claim: Both compilation paths (part_05.rs and compile/mod.rs) produce identical digests for identical inputs
notes: Proptest: generate random (source, contract) pairs, run through both paths, assert equal output. Kani: verify equivalence for a representative input. Ideally, deduplication makes this trivial.

domain_claim: YAML parser correctly parses and validates resource_contract section
notes: P2 priority. Kani: verify parser invariants for contract parsing. Proptest: generate valid/invalid YAML contract sections. Fuzz: cargo-fuzz the parser with malformed contract YAML. Current parser whitelist excludes resource_contract.

domain_claim: validate_resource_contract validates all 17 fields including max_transitions_per_tick
notes: After type merge, verify that max_transitions_per_tick=0 produces a validation error, and max_transitions_per_tick > HARD_MAX_TRANSITIONS_PER_TICK produces ResourceContractTooLarge. Kani: verify for boundary values.

domain_claim: Digest sensitivity to contract changes is tested by dedicated proptest
model_boundary: Test module covering canonical_digest contract sensitivity
notes: Proptest: for each of the 17 fields, randomly change the field value while keeping everything else constant, verify digest changes. Additionally, randomize all fields together and verify different contracts produce different digests.

domain_claim: Digest determinism holds across all contract values
notes: Kani: prove determinism for a bounded contract (all fields within small ranges). Proptest: call canonical_digest twice with same inputs, verify same output, for many random contracts.

domain_claim: canonical_digest(contract) and compute_policy_digest(contract) agree on contract identity
model_boundary: Relation between vb_compile canonical_digest and vb_storage compute_policy_digest
notes: Kani: verify that when the same ResourceContract is used, the contract portion of canonical_digest matches compute_policy_digest. They may use different hashing strategies (field-by-field vs postcard serialization), so they may produce different contract-portion hashes. The key invariant is: if contract_a ≠ contract_b, then both digests differ.

domain_claim: Hashed contract encoding is injective (no two different contracts produce the same contract hash)
notes: Verus: prove that the encoding function f: ResourceContract → [u8] is injective (contract_a ≠ contract_b ⇒ f(contract_a) ≠ f(contract_b)). This requires proving field-tagging prevents cross-field collisions. Kani: bounded verification for specific collision candidates.

domain_claim: compile_source_with_default(source) is equivalent to compile_source(source, ResourceContract::DEFAULT)
notes: Kani: verify that both paths produce identical CompiledWorkflow (same nodes, expressions, etc., and same digest). Proptest: random source, verify equivalence.
